name: Wearable VIR
full_name: Yanshan University wearable vascular interventional surgical robot
group: Yanshan University, Hebei Provincial Key Laboratory of Parallel Robot and Mechatronic System (Haoyang Yu, Hongbo Wang, Jianye Niu) with Fudan University Academy for Engineering & Technology
versions: 2023 wearable system (yu2023_wearable; received 2023, IJMRCAS 2024;20(1):e2616); its fuzzy-PID position controller comes from the group's earlier robot Yu et al., Appl. Sci. 2021;11(2):611 (ref. 24, not read); the same group's 2023 complex-coronary robot is A2's yu_complexcoronary_2023; 2021: H. Yu / H. Wang (Yanshan) VIS robot with force feedback and flexible clamping (Yu 2021 Appl. Sci. 11:611) and precise-delivery VIS robot with an operating-sleeve leader (Wang 2021 IEEE Access), possibly one robot (Chen 2023 Figs. 6(d), 9(a); Duan 2023 Table 1 row 4) (chen2023_operating; duan2023_progress); 2018: H. Y. Yu / H. B. Wang (Yanshan) master-slave system: master with an operating sleeve that slides and turns on a shaft (ball and V-groove decoupling), two encoders and a magnetic-particle clutch for force feedback; wire feeder that clamps, pushes and twists the device with a fixed, a promoting and a rotating finger; five servo motors; bench: feedback torque of the clutch calibrated with weights from 0.05 to 1 N m, about linear in the clutch current (Yu 2018 RCAR, Secs. II, IV, Figs. 2, 6, 11); the group's 2011-2015 mechanisms (X. Yang, H. Wang; Zhao 2022 Table 1 row 8b, Belikov 2024 Fig. 6 YA) are earlier versions, not read (yu2018_master; zhao2022_remote; belikov2024_evolution)
target_anatomy: coronary (PCI): radial artery to the coronary arteries in a human vessel model, femoral access to the right coronary artery in a pig (yu2023_wearable Sec. 2.3.3-2.3.4)
devices_driven: one guidewire or one catheter at a time; catheter and guidewire cannot be driven together (Sec. 4). Animal study: Cordis ATW guidewire (ATW-595-ME014) through a manually placed MPA1 8F catheter (Sec. 2.3.4)
n_dof_detail: 3 device DOF: clamp, push/pull, twist (Sec. 2.1, Sec. 5); plus DM pitch set by a linear actuator and position on a lockable slideway of the wearable frame (Sec. 2.1.2, Fig. 6)
translation_detail: clamp-relay: fixing module (F1, F2) holds the wire while the clamping module (C1, C2) on a screw-driven slider pushes, then they swap ('reciprocating delivery'; Sec. 2.1.2, Figs. 7-8); propulsion DC motor 26SYK55.24 (Sec. 2.2.1)
rotation_detail: wedge-shaped gripper closed by a crank-rocker and spring, rotated with the clamped wire through a gear set by a Maxon RE13 motor (Sec. 2.1.2, Fig. 9)
force_sensing: slave: pressure sensor (SBT674-10 N) under the clamping module, a lever with arm ratio l1/l2 = 3 amplifies the delivery resistance 3x (Sec. 2.1.2, Fig. 10); master: torque sensor (DSN-206) in the handle drive (Sec. 2.2.1)
haptics_leader: custom 3-DOF handle (operating manipulator): slide and rotation read by encoders, three-button squeeze read by a thin-film sensor (Flexiforce) sets the clamp; a servo motor with torque sensor drags the handle, velocity-force mapping slows it as delivery resistance rises (Sec. 2.1.1, 2.2.2, Figs. 2-5, 14)
imaging_compat: used under a C-arm angiography system in the pig study (Sec. 2.3.4, Fig. 19); radiolucency N.R.
sterility: driven gear shaft and gripper held by a magnetic cover, removed and replaced after surgery for sterilisation (Sec. 2.1.2); drape N.R.
validation_detail: bench: 5 push and 5 twist master-slave tracking runs, 5 force-feedback runs (Sec. 2.3.1-2.3.2); human vessel model: 4 untrained testers x 3 targets x 3 trials, all 12 target deliveries within 60 s by the 3rd trial (Table 1); animal: 1 Bama pig (SIAT), guidewire to the right coronary artery, 3 robotic vs 3 manual deliveries, delivery time +2.46 %, operator exposure time -71.50 % (Sec. 2.3.4, 3.4, Fig. 23)
key_numbers: static error 0.048 mm (0.019 %), relative dynamic error 0.204 % over 250 mm; rotation static error 1.259 deg (0.682 %), relative dynamic 2.217 % over 400 deg; force-feedback error mean 0.021 N, max 0.055 N (mean 2.566 %, max 6.746 %) (Sec. 3.1-3.2); 5 motors in master + slave; wireless NRF24L01 master-slave link (Sec. 2.2.1)
